key_insight: LLM reasoning performance is reflected in small-world functional connectivity: higher small-world index aligns with better reasoning ability.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical structural signal for diagnosing and preserving reasoning capacity when pruning or allocating sparsity in LLMs.
method: Build functional graphs from attention-head activation similarity.
Measure small-world index plus head-level core and bridge scores.
Use these scores to guide hierarchical sparsity allocation (SWA).
evidence_signal: Across six LLMs and training checkpoints, higher SWI correlated with better fluid reasoning, and SWA reduced WikiText perplexity by up to 20% while preserving performance better than competing allocations.
watch_item: The structural signal is correlational, so its usefulness may depend on model family, checkpoint stage, and how attention similarities are constructed.
paper_title: Looking Inside LLMs: Small-World Connectivity as a Signature of Reasoning Performance
